newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Experts discuss air safety in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Experts discuss air safety in Africa.

text.p: Airline experts and representatives began a two-day meeting on air safety in Africa on Thursday at the headquarters of the Francophone air safety agency ASECNA.
Youssoufa Mahamat, acting director of ASECNA, told delegates that recent incidents were a matter of great concern in the industry and to its users.
Delegates included representatives from the 15 member countries and from airlines from outside Africa that ply routes in the region.
"We are here because we are concerned about air safety," Trevor Fox, director for infrastructure in the Africa region of the International Air Transport Association (IATA), told Reuters.
He said that his organisation's concerns focused on the system of high frequency communications between pilots and air traffic controllers in use in the ASECNA region.

"High frequency communication is not the most reliable means of communication between pilots and controllers. The most reliable way is VHF. We have been pressing for a long time to have such facilities implemented in this region," he added.
The latest plane crash in Africa to hit the headlines was a charter flight that crashed in ASECNA member Senegal on February 1, killing 23 passengers.
Cameroon and non-members Nigeria and Zaire have all experienced fatal crashes over the past couple of years.
